measured.order2_guard: tot2[h2] checked before the cnt2 row is touched — rows materialize only for contexts with history (resident cost tracks distinct contexts already)

parity_anchor.note: the judge core alone is at tiktoken parity (PLAN_v0.8 attribution: 9.6 vs 9.8 MB/s); the lane-level gap is patcher bookkeeping + probe traffic, not the per-order tables

decision.lever: per-order tables sized to distinct-context counts
decision.gate: >= 5% lane-level improvement on the quiet-box protocol, else declined
reasons: orders 3-5 ALREADY use the sized open-addressing map (tmap grows with distinct contexts) — the lever exists only for orders 1-2

orders 1-2 are DENSE DIRECT arrays (cnt1 256 KB, tot2 256 KB — L2-resident) indexed with zero indirection; a distinct-count-sized variant of the same model must add a hash->slot indirection to the hottest per-byte loop, strictly more cache misses
shrinking the slice widths instead would change the model and the ids — forbidden by the 1.0 bit-freeze (exact-lane ids/spans/snapshot frozen within 1.x)

the judge core is at tiktoken parity in isolation, so even a perfect table win cannot move the lane >= 5% — the remaining sequential gap is patcher bookkeeping + probe memory traffic (PLAN_v0.9 P1 baseline)
the 64 MB order-2 region is virtual and guarded; resident cost already tracks distinct contexts (measured: 9226 nonzero tot2 rows of 65536 after 1 MB of real text)
decision.ship: no code change; the sized-map design ships for orders 3-5 (it always has) and the dense direct design ships for orders 1-2
